text:
acme-eng: hi team — during a deploy our app hit a ~5m traffic spike and we started getting 429s with "burst_exhausted". burst credits dropped to 0 in ~30s, we expected smoothing to absorb this. account: acme-inc, project: web-search, region: us-west. any ideas?

sara-support: thanks — can you paste an example request/response and the request id or a time range? I can escalate to SRE once we have that.

acme-eng: sure, here's a condensed repro we ran around 2025-06-09T15:12Z (request id: rq_0a1b2c3d):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \  
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \  
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \  
  -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","input":"<many short queries>"}'
```

Response:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate_limit",
    "message": "burst_exhausted",
    "retry_after": 6
  },
  "request_id": "rq_0a1b2c3d"
}
```

We were sending ~350 rps for ~40s, concurrency ~80.

sara-support: got it — are you on Pay-as-you-go or a reserved plan? Also can you confirm whether "burst_smoothing" is toggled in the project settings?

acme-eng: PAYG. Console shows "smoothing: auto" (not explicitly ON). Not sure what that means for the spike.

eng-sre-jack: SRE here — quick context: burst credits are bucketed per project and refill at a steady rate tied to your baseline capacity. Short intense spikes can exhaust that bucket quickly. 

Smoothing is an edge-side buffer that will try to spread request tokens over a smoothing_window (default 30s) but it needs headroom in the bucket to function. If a spike consumes both the bucket + smoothing buffer, you'll still get 429s.

Typical mitigations: lower client concurrency, add exponential backoff with jitter, enable/expand smoothing_window (e.g., 60s), or move to Reserved capacity if this pattern is regular. :point_up:

sara-support: you can toggle smoothing in Console -> Projects -> Quotas. API route if you prefer:

```http
PATCH /v1/projects/{project_id}
Content-Type: application/json
{ "burst_smoothing": true, "smoothing_window": 60 }
```

acme-eng: we flipped smoothing on just now and set 60s but we still saw 429s in the following minute. Does smoothing not apply immediately?

eng-sre-jack: it applies immediately for new requests, but it doesn't retroactively refill consumed credits. If the spike already drained the bucket, smoothing can only spread tokens that remain and any incoming refill. Refill is continuous but limited (it won't instantly top you up).

product-anya: product note — smoothing reduces short-term variance but isn't a replacement for capacity. For unpredictable microbursts we recommend one of:
- Reserved capacity for headroom
- Client backpressure + retries
- Prompt/response sizing to reduce tokens per request

We're tracking an improvement to surface "burst headroom" in Console so teams see how close they are to exhausting credits. I'll file that as a product task.

sara-support: in the short term we can do two things: 1) run telemetry to confirm exact depletion timeline (can you share logs/ timestamps), 2) offer a one-time emergency top-up while you evaluate Reserved capacity — billing needs a request.

billing-bot: To request a temporary credits top-up, reply with `request_topup acme-inc` and include the account owner email. Support will route to billing for approval.

acme-eng: thanks — filing `request_topup acme-inc` now and uploading logs to the ticket. For mitigation we will also add client-side concurrency limits and longer backoff.

eng-sre-jack: small client example for backoff (JS):

```js
async function callWithBackoff(req) {
  let attempts = 0;
  while (attempts < 5) {
    const res = await fetch('/v1/generate', req);
    if (res.status !== 429) return res;
    const retry = Math.min(1000 * 2 ** attempts + Math.random() * 300, 60000);
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, retry));
    attempts++;
  }
  throw new Error('max retries hit');
}
```

sara-support: action items: I will open INC-205111 (support -> eng-sre) to gather full traces and ask Product for the Console visibility ticket. acme-eng to attach logs + confirm whether attack/spike is expected pattern.

acme-eng: will do, thanks everyone. very helpful. :thumbsup:

product-anya: follow-up: I'll add a note to upcoming roadmap for an alert when projected burst bucket < 10% for 5m.

sara-support: closing the loop here — please post the INC number once you upload logs and we'll keep this thread updated.

acme-eng: uploaded logs to INC-205111. thanks again!
